name: casey
caption:
WE FIRED THE COACH OF THE YEAR 🎮🏀

• 2017-18: 59-23, a franchise record, and the No. 1 seed in the East for the first time
• Then Cleveland swept us, 0-4, in the second round
• May 11, 2018: we fired Dwane Casey
• June 25, 2018: he was named NBA Coach of the Year
• June 14, 2018: we promoted assistant Nick Nurse. In his first season, we won the 2019 title

Right call? 👇

beats.head: 59 WINS
beats.name: CASEY
beats.vo: We won fifty-nine games. Then Cleveland swept us. So we fired our coach.
beats.dlg: 59 WINS. SWEPT BY CLEVELAND.|SO WE FIRED THE COACH.

beats.head: 45 DAYS LATER
beats.name: CASEY
beats.vo: Forty-five days later, Dwane Casey was named Coach of the Year.
beats.dlg: 45 DAYS LATER:|NBA COACH OF THE YEAR.

beats.head: THE NEW GUY
beats.name: NURSE
beats.vo: We promoted his assistant, Nick Nurse. In his first season, we won the title.
beats.dlg: WE PROMOTED NICK NURSE.|YEAR ONE: CHAMPIONS.

beats.head: RIGHT CALL?
beats.vo: Was firing the Coach of the Year the right call? Comment below.
beats.dlg: FIRE HIM OR KEEP HIM?|COMMENT BELOW.

facts.claim: 2017-18 Raptors: 59-23, a franchise record for wins (59), first time as the 1st seed (No. 1) in the East; lost to the Cleveland Cavaliers 0-4 in the Conference Semifinals (second round).
On May 11, 2018, Casey was fired as the Raptors' head coach; he won NBA Coach of the Year at the 2018 NBA Awards on June 25, 2018, 45 days later.
2018 NBA Awards held June 25, 2018; NBA Coach of the Year: Dwane Casey, Toronto Raptors.
On June 14, 2018, the Raptors promoted assistant Nick Nurse to head coach; he won the 2019 NBA championship in his 1st (first) season (head coach 2018-2022).
